fix(edit-chrome): a placement's chrome names are its own, so an edit beside it renames nothing (#695)

* fix(edit-chrome): a placement's chrome names are its own, so an edit beside it renames nothing (brandon-unfiled-3248.5bfl)

Edit chrome spelled every insert slot, removal, configure entry, draft
variable and setting control from one walk counter shared over the preset
tree, so adding, removing or moving a placement shifted the name of every
control after it, and an open + library, its page cursor or an open
configure list landed on a neighbour after the reload. Every name is now
spelled from the placement it serves through chromeIdent, an injective
base-36 spelling of the id that is a fixed point of ident, and the counter
is gone.

The default-menu bytes snapshot regenerates for the new link names; its
plain text is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(edit-chrome): a pick at the row's leading ✚ closes its library, whose gap the pick renames (brandon-unfiled-3248.5bfl)

A pick at a before gap makes the new placement the row's first content, so the
reload names the leading gap after it and the library's state key is declared
no more. Nothing closes an undeclared key, so it stayed open and reopened on
its own when the anchor led its row again. The leading library now closes on
pick, while its key is still declared; an after gap keeps its name across its
own pick and stays open.

The default-menu-bytes 'one + opened' entry moves: each leading-library option
link now carries the close write after its layout op.

* fix(edit-chrome): a layout edit releases every state key it ends, so a leading-✚ pick lands without a click error (brandon-unfiled-3248.5bfl)

The leading ✚'s close-on-pick ran after the layout op had reloaded the config,
when its key was no longer declared, so the state gate refused it and every
pick there showed a click error. The layout-op verb now releases, in the same
click, every session key the config declared before the edit and no longer
declares: the leading library's key after a pick renames its gap, and every
key a removed placement's chrome held, which a later placement minted with the
freed id would otherwise inherit open. The per-gap close-on-pick is gone; the
default-menu-bytes 'one + opened' entry returns to its links without it.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(release): set `package.json` to 1.212.2 [skip ci]

## [1.212.2](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.212.1...v1.212.2) (2026-11-08)

### Bug Fixes

* **daemon:** the lane edge takes the daemon's claude-input edge (candybar-testing-ihvy.izc.ubq) ([#698](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/698)) ([3f5670d](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/3f5670db72be5ec2abd20fa416f132125685c675))

fix(watchers): a probe that sees no ctime move gives no verdict, every probe logs where it is made, and check judges folders by its own probe (brandon-unfiled-3248.0463)

- No ctime movement inside the bound is no evidence either way, so the
  probe answers unprobed with the reason, logged as a warning, instead
  of supplied.
- probeBirthtimeIn takes the process's logger and logs the verdict
  itself, so the daemon, the page, the demo and the test daemon all
  report it from one place; the server's own line is gone.
- prepareConfig (check, gallery) builds its watch registry over its own
  probed disk, the one production watch owner left on the unprobed one.
- package.json devEngines states the repository's Node floor, which
  jest's module.registerHooks needs (22.15 / 23.5), apart from the
  package's runtime engines.

brandon-unfiled-3248.0463

fix(watchers): the daemon probes birth time at boot, in its state directory, and builds its disk over the verdict (brandon-unfiled-3248.0463)

The probe ran ambiently on any process's first stat, on the real clock and
in the spawning shell's TMPDIR, behind two disabled lint rules. A process
main now probes once with its own clock in a folder it owns, logs the
verdict (warn when unprobed), and hands the daemon a disk built over it; no
CLI process or client tick pays for a probe. Jest's global hooks resolve a
`.js` specifier to its TypeScript source as a test's registry does, so src
keeps one import spelling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(watchers): a folder's identity stays put across child writes where birth time is a ctime copy (brandon-unfiled-3248.0463)

Where statx fails, libuv copies ctime into birth time for the life of the
process, and a directory's ctime moves on every child create, remove or
rename, so every write in a watched folder read as another folder. The
disk adapter now probes once per process, on its first stat, whether birth
time moves with ctime, and Stat and FolderIdentity carry no birth time
(null) where the host copies ctime or statx reports 0. The daemon logs the
verdict at startup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(git): the real-git case for the daemon's environment is an adapter case, under test/integration (brandon-unfiled-3248.i3ek)

It drives real git through the system launcher, which the test lint
admits only in the adapter tiers; it reached it through worldOf, past the
rule. What it proves is git's own behaviour, so it belongs with the
adapters. [LAW:effects-at-boundaries]

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(git): each session's git reads answer for its own directory (brandon-unfiled-3248.i3ek)

A daemon spawned from an environment carrying GIT_DIR or another of git's
repository variables (a hook, vcsh, yadm) passed it to every git read, so
every bar showed the spawning shell's repository. The daemon now asks git
for those names once at its process edge, before its lease, bounded at 2 s,
and runs in a world whose environment is the process's without them. An ask
that fails keeps the inherited environment and draws a git-env warning on
every bar; a git that is not installed names none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(diagnostics): a list with nothing wrong in it draws ℹ N in blue, not an amber ⚠ (brandon-unfiled-3248.gm3h)

A third diagnostic level, info, carried in one level table (rank, the
indicator's glyph, the colours). An update offer, a repository question and
the lane handoff line are info. The indicator wears the list's worst level
and the list runs worst first, so its click opens a message of that level.
A failed update act is a plain warning of its own beside the offer, so the
failure still raises an amber ⚠ while the offer keeps its identity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cache): each catch-up turn takes the most recently used due entry as the map stands (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A session drawn during the walk is now re-read on the next turn, not
where its entry stood when the batch began. A turn clears its handle
before it reloads and arms only when none is armed, so a batch started
inside a turn leaves one walker. A throw is logged with its stack.

fix(cache): a catch-up turn is its own error boundary and walks most recently used first (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A walk turn runs from setImmediate, outside the watcher registry's
try/catch, so a reload that threw there reached uncaughtException and
shut the daemon down. The turn now logs the throw and arms the next.

The walk takes the most recently used entry first, so the bar in front
of the user is re-read on the first turn. The due set is a Set: every
due entry always reloads for the latest batch's cause, which the armed
turn carries.

fix(cache): a catch-up reloads one entry per turn, so requests are answered between entries (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

When file events resumed after a stall, or the repo answers moved, the
render cache reloaded every entry in one synchronous turn. A reload that
keeps its state still resolves, validates and keys the whole chain, so
105 entries held the live daemon's loop for 1.7s on a calm machine and
11s on a loaded one, and every client waiting behind it hung up (the
EPIPE bursts in daemon.log).

The walk now takes one due entry per turn of the loop. Any reload clears
its entry's due mark, a drop clears a dropped entry's, a reload that
throws ends only its own turn, and close cancels the armed turn. The
render cache's stats count the entries still due.
